criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: The introduction thoroughly addresses the primary mission, environmental context, and societal necessity of monitoring coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef. The choice of a single microsatellite is well-justified based on the timescales of coral bleaching events. Key operational users (AIMS) and customer stakeholders (GBRMPA, CSIRO, BoM) are clearly identified. Strong supporting citations from scientific literature and official bodies are integrated throughout.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program for the reef

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: The mission design is exceptionally detailed and technically rigorous. Launch provider trade-offs, orbital mechanics, sun-synchronous drift rate calculations, ground track geometry, and access statistics are derived both analytically and through STK simulations. Payload sizing, daily data generation, downlink margins, and drag-sail orbital decay calculations are mathematically coherent and accurate. All required operational parameters (manoeuvres, duration, EOL deorbiting) are fully covered.

criteria.reasoning: The conclusion provides a concise, effective summary of all critical design outputs and quantitative performance metrics. It excels by providing an honest, insightful engineering evaluation of the design's limitations, including launch vehicle readiness risks, scaling of fluid lensing technology, ground station communication upgrades, and the revisit cadence trade-off.

The technical writing is lucid, concise, and grammatically impeccable throughout.

technical_issues.issue: The launch azimuth formula sin(beta) = cos(i)/cos(phi) yields the inertial burnout azimuth; calculating the topocentric launch azimuth requires correcting for the eastward tangential velocity of Earth's rotation.
A quantitative RF link budget for the 50 Mbit/s X-band payload downlink and S-band TT&C link was omitted.

overall: This is an outstanding, professional-grade space mission design report. It satisfies all task requirements and rubric criteria to an exceptionally high standard. The technical analyses—combining first-principles orbital mechanics, link and data budgeting, atmospheric drag modeling, and STK verification—are rigorous and clearly communicated, complemented by a candid discussion of engineering trade-offs and limitations.

feedback.summary: You have delivered an outstanding, professional-grade space mission design report for ZYZZsat. Your technical analyses effectively integrate first-principles orbital mechanics, STK simulation verification, and realistic engineering trade-offs. The report thoroughly details operational context, launch options, and EOL disposal. To elevate your work to industry-standard rigor, ensure rotational corrections are incorporated into launch azimuth derivations and include quantitative RF link budgets alongside your data volume sizing.
